primarySources.title: Yosemite Valley — Yosemite National Park (U.S. National Park Service)
primarySources.captureText:
# Yosemite Valley
Yosemite Valley, home to many of the famous cliffs and waterfalls that make Yosemite National Park famous is accessible by car and bus all year.
## Points of Interest
Yosemite Valley is home to most of the park’s famous waterfalls. The best time to see them is during spring runoff; they have little or no water in late summer and fall. Tunnel View provides one of the most famous views of Yosemite Valley. From here you can see El Capitan and Bridalveil Fall rising from Yosemite Valley, with Half Dome in the background. The viewpoint is at the east end of the Wawona Tunnel along Wawona Road.

primarySources.title: Granite — Yosemite National Park (U.S. National Park Service)
primarySources.captureText:
# Granite
Granite dominates the geology of Yosemite National Park. The park boundary frames a landscape composed almost entirely of granite and containing some of the most iconic rock formations on earth. The southeast face of El Capitan includes the older and lighter-colored El Capitan and Taft granites, with darker Diorite of North America. Plutons are named after famous landmarks dominantly made of their rock; examples include Half Dome Granodiorite and El Capitan Granite. Yosemite is known throughout the world for its exceptional high cliffs and rounded domes.

primarySources.title: Geology — Yellowstone National Park (U.S. National Park Service)
primarySources.captureText:
# Geology
Yellowstone was established as the world’s first national park primarily because of its extraordinary geysers, hot springs, mudpots, and steam vents. The park has more than 10,000 hydrothermal features, including approximately 500 geysers, and the largest concentration of active geysers in the world—more than half of the world’s total.

primarySources.title: Geologic Formations — Grand Canyon National Park (U.S. National Park Service)
primarySources.captureText:
# Geologic Formations
The Grand Canyon of the Colorado River is a world-renowned showplace of geology. The Colorado River carved the Grand Canyon into four plateaus of the Colorado Plateau Province. Its mile-high walls display a largely undisturbed cross section of Earth’s crust extending back some two billion years.

primarySources.title: Hydrologic Activity — Everglades National Park (U.S. National Park Service)
primarySources.captureText:
# Hydrologic Activity
The phrase “River of Grass” was coined by Marjory Stoneman Douglas in 1947. Everglades National Park protects part of the Greater Everglades, the largest freshwater marsh in the United States, and includes terrestrial, estuarine, and marine habitats. Water flows slowly through the broad, shallow wetland system.
